description.narrative:
This pilot project will be implemented in 4 regions in Colombia which are experiencing high levels of violence and high levels of violence against women where women regularly do not report cases of violence due to fear of reprisal from the aggressor or for lack of trust in the state institutions responsible for investigating these crimes. The main focus of the work will take place with indigenous women’s groups in Apartadó and Cauca.
In this one year pilot project, the partners will focus on strengthening the capacity of local and regional women's networks / indigenous groups, so that they are aware of their rights, legal national and international frameworks that promote and protect women's rights and are able to participate in decision making and peace building processes at local, regional and national level. Furthermore, in order to promote public policies addressing the causes of violence against women, the project will use an educational tool developed by SNPS/Caritas Colombia during a recent UN Women funded project which raised awareness of Law 1257 on the elimination of violence against women and was used to train representatives of local justice administrations.
Furthermore the issue of mining and gender will be explored.
The project will involve both men and women in order to improve gender relations at community level and encourage a greater participation of women in decision making processes. A learning exchange will also be organised in order to share experiences and learning between excluded groups (indigenous and displaced groups).
In Apartadó and Northern Cauca, the project will focus on strengthening the role of Embera and Nasa indigenous women within the indigenous councils (cabildos) so that they can influence local community development plans. In Barrancabermeja, women’s groups will be strengthened to influence public policies and in San Vicente the focus will be on women victims of the armed conflict.
